hypothesis: If the claim holds, strictly freshwater fish species will almost never be native to two distant continents, while sharing between river systems within a continent will be common.
pass_criterion: Among primary and secondary freshwater fish species (diadromous and marine-tolerant species excluded) the fraction native to both Africa and South America, and to both Australia and Eurasia, is <= 1%; within-continent sharing across at least two river basins is >= 10% of species.
fail_criterion: More than 5% of strictly freshwater species are native on two distant continents.
interpretation: 'Same species in fresh waters of distant continents' means the same species natively present in two widely separated continents. Introduced species must be excluded, and euryhaline or diadromous species are outside Darwin's freshwater scope. 'Ranging capriciously' within continents is read as a species occurring in some but not all river basins.
